garage.name: Whip Equipped Garage
garage.category: Story hub, workshop, and tire bay
garage.tagline: Every vehicle has a before and after.
garage.description: McCluster, Majid, and Gunny anchor an enterable garage where district stories meet the existing Whip Equipped chapters.
garage.backstory: The garage is a new playable setting for the existing fictional story, presented as a visit before the finale. Its workshop and tire bay give the cast a practical reason to gather. The chapter hub opens the separately maintained screenplay and road-years material rather than replacing long scenes with short NPC exchanges.
ads: WHIP EQUIPPED. Pull into the story.
The next job starts with the whole situation.

interior.style: Familiar working garage with a tire bay and chapter desk
interior.description: A workshop bench, tire stack, and three gathering spots keep the garage readable. A chapter desk leads into the existing long-form story; it is not a replacement for its before/song/after structure.

story.chapterContract: Each chapter preserves before-dialogue 2× song length, the complete uninterrupted song, and after-dialogue 2× song length. Adjacent scenes are not counted twice; the music video has its own expressive staging.
story.mrLockChanger: Keep both perspectives: McCluster’s legitimate service work and the cousin’s criminal misuse of the tablet received from him, with police anxiety, imitation, and humor. This is not a technical theft tutorial.
story.alana: Alana is the same loved character from Test Drive, personifies Atlanta becoming a trap, and dies in Tears Won’t Fall. She is not a permanent post-ending city resident; later appearances require clearly framed memory or subjective imagery.
story.roadYearEvidence: The three initial camper/G20/Econoline entries are owner recollections, tentatively 2024. Photos, dates, transaction amounts, and costs need later reconciliation; the two van sales remain different deals.

garageCrew.name: McCluster
garageCrew.role: Garage owner and Whip Equipped story contact
garageCrew.backstory: McCluster is the existing fictional Whip Equipped protagonist. The garage puts his practical work, relationships, and business ambitions in the same room rather than turning him into a detached mission dispenser. Current story canon preserves his legitimate service work alongside knowingly accepted criminal capital and the choices that follow. The city does not rewrite that tension as either complete innocence or a claim about the owner’s real company. His dialogue here belongs to a chapter-selection visit before the finale. The road-years material provides separate remembered legitimate flips whose approximate dates and costs remain qualified in their source documents. Ages, historical origin, likeness, and any new personal biography remain unassigned by this city expansion.
garageCrew.personality: Resourceful, restless, humorous; wants ownership of his work and must answer for his choices.

dialogue.greeting: You made it to the shop. Pull up. There’s work on the lift and a story behind most of it.

topics.label: What makes this the home spot?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Everybody on this block sends people here.

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: Because a vehicle still has to work after somebody finishes talking about it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: And the people?

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: Same problem, harder diagnosis. Majid checks the plan. Gunny asks who actually agreed to it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: What do you do?

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: Try to build something I can stand behind when the noise dies down.

topics.label: What is behind Mr. Lock Changer?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: That tablet story sounds different depending on who is telling it.

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: Exactly. My service work is one thing. My cousin got a tablet from me and made his own choices with it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: So the police anxiety belongs to another angle too?

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: Keep your eyes on who is holding the tool and what job they’re really doing.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Same object, different intentions.

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: And the joke gets darker when somebody thinks looking like the business means doing the business.

topics.label: Tell me about the van run.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: You really lived out of a van while flipping it?

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: That G20 got me through a stretch. Michigan, down to Georgia, back up. Making gas money as I went.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: And then the green van?

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: Different vehicle. A lead from the G20 turned into the Econoline sale. Keep those two deals straight.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Do you have the whole timeline?

lines.speaker: McCluster
lines.text: Pieces. Photos will help put the dates back where they belong. The road stays vivid even when the numbers need checking.

dialogue.farewell: Stay a minute if you need to. Just don’t promise the next job before you hear the whole situation.

garageCrew.name: Majid
garageCrew.role: Garage regular, advisor, and roadside story contact
garageCrew.backstory: Majid is an existing Whip Equipped character whose role includes advising independent money before an exit from the criminal entanglement. The owner’s road recollections also identify him as a supportive voice during the lean van-driving period, while his brother helped tow the earlier camper. This city version uses those established roles without inventing a birthplace, age, mechanic’s qualification, or historical transaction record. He can be funny and skeptical in the garage, but the point of his presence is continuity: the person supporting the protagonist on the road is available when another big plan arrives. New city dialogue dramatizes that relationship. It does not upgrade approximate recollections into verified costs or use legitimate flips as corroboration of fictional crime.
garageCrew.personality: Steady, candid, supportive; asks how a plan works when the excitement wears off.

dialogue.greeting: What’s the plan, and what’s the plan if the first plan eats all the gas money?

topics.label: What were those roadside calls like?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: McCluster says you were on the phone through the van run.

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: You stay with your people when the road starts feeling bigger than the plan.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Were you giving directions?

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: Sometimes. Sometimes you just need another voice while you figure out the next stop.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Sounds like a lot of uncertainty.

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: It was. Don’t edit that out just because the flip eventually has a selling price.

topics.label: What counts as a good flip?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Buy cheap, sell higher. Simple, right?

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: Then remember the tow, the gas, the flight, the days, and the ride home.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: McCluster has rough numbers for those.

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: Rough numbers are a place to start. Let the records help before you call it exact profit.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: What matters beyond the number?

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: Whether you can make the next move without somebody owning the decision for you.

topics.label: Why keep talking about independent money?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Why not leave a bad arrangement as soon as you hate it?

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: Because wanting out and being able to stand on your own are different problems.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: So wait forever?

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: No. Build the way out while you can still choose what it looks like.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: And if somebody keeps changing the terms?

lines.speaker: Majid
lines.text: Then stop confusing their next promise with your own plan.

dialogue.farewell: Check in when you get there. A successful deal includes the trip home.

garageCrew.name: Gunny
garageCrew.backstory: Gunny is the existing story character whose commitments protect autonomy over crews and decisions. The city assigns him a practical point of contact at the garage without inventing an earlier technical career or making him the unconfirmed mechanic behind every repair. He listens to requests, asks who is available, and refuses to treat another person’s time as already promised. That makes him useful in a district where almost every business is advertising more certainty than it possesses. His new conversations connect a funny booking dispute to the story’s more serious concern with who controls a person’s labor and choices. His age, origin, and precise appearance remain unresolved rather than receiving biographical filler.
garageCrew.personality: Direct, grounded, wry; values a clear commitment and the freedom to make it.

dialogue.greeting: Tell me what needs doing. Then we’ll find out who actually agreed to do it.

topics.label: Can I borrow your crew?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Can you send your people to help with a shoot?

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: I can ask people. Start there.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I thought you handled the crew.

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: Handling a schedule doesn’t make somebody mine.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: So what do you need?

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: The job, the time, the pay, and enough room for somebody to answer honestly.

topics.label: What is wrong with this block’s bookings?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Three shops promised the same van.

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: Did any of them talk to the person holding the keys?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: They talked to each other.

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: Then they built a very confident conversation around an absent vehicle.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: How do we fix it?

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: Start with Beatrice. The keys usually have a better understanding of the schedule than the advertisement.

topics.label: What does standing on business mean here?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Everybody keeps saying they stand on business.

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: Then ask what happens when the promise gets inconvenient.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: That’s when you find out?

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: That’s when the slogan has to put shoes on.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: And the shop?

lines.speaker: Gunny
lines.text: We’ve got enough work without making somebody else’s choice for them. Be clear about what you’re committing to.

dialogue.farewell: If the plan changes, tell the people carrying it.

beats.title: The Aftermath
beats.summary: Dave wakes beside four people who will not wake. The shoes are impossibly clean.
paragraphs: A failing streetlight catches the boarded windows of Ashline Works. Inside, Dave comes to on the concrete. Four people lie dead nearby; a bag of cash sits open. He cannot account for what happened.

He looks down at the pristine Robbery 1s. The neighborhood has a story about those shoes: their wearers finish in a grave or a cell unless they let go. Dave removes them, grabs them by the laces, and runs barefoot into the night.
An old head at a nearby dice game recognizes the pair. His warning follows Dave through the alleys. Whatever the shoes promised, Dave wants no part of it now.
beats.objective: Find Ashline Works and begin Dave’s story.

beats.title: A Pair in the Bin
beats.summary: Dave throws the pair away. By morning, Malik finds what looks like a way out.
paragraphs: Dave reaches a donation bin, drops the Robbery 1s inside, and leaves. The shoes have changed hands before anyone has agreed to a bargain.

Morning brings buses, opening storefronts, and Malik walking in sneakers with loose soles. He spots the pair in the bin, checks the street, and slips them on. A chill passes through him; his stance changes.
Kiara notices both the shoes and the new attitude. Across the street, Harold notices something else: this is the original pair. Malik does not yet understand what Harold recognizes.
beats.objective: Visit the donation bin near Last Light Market.
beats.propPlacement: Authored donation-bin prop on clear land outside retained building footprints and mapped road widths.

beats.title: The First Door
beats.summary: The shopkeeper recognizes the shoes before Malik understands their reputation.
paragraphs: Harold offers to buy the pair. When Malik refuses, he tells him to test their reputation at the corner store. Kiara stays close, already uneasy.
The shopkeeper sees Malik’s feet and his welcome turns to fear. He gives away the snacks, empties the day’s takings, and asks Malik to keep other people from shaking down the shop.
Malik calls it an easy errand. Kiara sees a threshold he has crossed. Harold offers a place at the neighborhood trials, while Kiara reminds Malik that her aunt has legitimate work available.
beats.objective: Approach the market and hear what happened at the counter.

beats.title: Rent by Friday
beats.summary: Mama’s bills and Kiara’s offer show what Malik is trying to escape, and what he could still choose.
paragraphs: At home, Mama’s desk is covered in late notices. She studies the new shoes, then her son. Her first concern is where he has been; his attention keeps returning to the unpaid rent.
She wants him fed, in school, and home safely. Kiara’s offer of a real shift is still there. Neither of them can promise an instant answer to every bill.
Malik sits with the pair and decides to find out what being special will pay. The next morning, he heads toward the trials instead of his ordinary day.
beats.objective: Visit Northline Walkups and hear Malik’s family scene.

beats.title: The Block Olympics
beats.summary: An alley competition turns impossible luck into neighborhood fame.
paragraphs: A crooked banner, folding-table officials, a whistle, and an overworked speaker turn the yard into a ridiculous local stadium. Harold watches Malik arrive. Kiara has come looking for him.

The Robbery 1s carry Malik through extraordinary feats: a single bound over the fence, an impossible cuff reversal, and three sevens at dice. He insists on paying during the bodega receipt challenge, but even a polite purchase makes the shopkeeper afraid.

During the money weigh-in and the final dodging circle, the crowd turns Malik into a celebrity. Kiara sees fear disguised as generosity. Harold announces that Malik has qualified for real work. Malik asks what it pays.
beats.objective: Reach Common Yard and follow the neighborhood trials.

beats.title: The Promotion
beats.summary: Mr. GREAT makes the organization look like an employer and Malik look like a recruit.
paragraphs: In the club’s backroom, folding chairs face a whiteboard welcoming new enforcement. A clipboard, a lanyard, and a probationary badge turn a dangerous offer into absurd workplace ceremony.
Ocho Gr8, addressed as Mr. GREAT, assigns Malik to collect neighborhood dues with Harold. The instructions are about hierarchy and obedience. Malik is being welcomed for his usefulness.

The first route makes the job seem effortless until a resistant man exposes how quickly Malik’s anger is growing. Back in the car, Harold praises him. Mr. GREAT studies the shoes without explaining what he sees.
beats.objective: Visit Night Shift Club and hear the promotion scene.

beats.title: Legend Tax
beats.summary: Fear clears the hallway. A $15,000 bag earns Malik $1,000.
paragraphs: Malik returns home with money. Mama knows the bills are real, but she will not confuse cash with safety. The next day, neighbors lower their eyes as he passes.
At school, classmates make room and his closest friend looks away. The attention that felt like belonging in the yard feels like isolation here. Malik leaves early and returns to Harold.

That night, the organization counts $15,000 from the route and gives Malik $1,000. On the walk home, he compares the two amounts. His need to help Mama is turning into a conviction that the whole operation should answer to him.
beats.objective: Go to Brickline School and hear the cost of Malik’s reputation.

beats.title: New Turf · The Stairwell
beats.summary: The first new route refuses to make room for Harold and Malik.
paragraphs: Harold warns Malik that today’s stops are different. Under a concrete stairwell, the waiting circle closes instead of welcoming them. A local leader rejects the organization’s claim on the place.

The confrontation turns physical. Malik moves with the shoes’ uncanny timing, takes the envelope, and walks out with more confidence than caution. Harold is still calling it a collection; the neighborhood is living through the consequences.
beats.objective: Reach the walkups’ stairwell approach for the first New Turf scene.

beats.title: New Turf · The Laundry
beats.summary: Dryers drown out the backroom until the encounter spills into the street.
paragraphs: Behind the laundromat, a low basement room is too crowded and too tense. Harold notices before Malik does. The door closes behind them.

The meeting breaks into chaos among laundry carts and folding tables. Malik’s unnatural reflexes get them through, and he pulls Harold away from danger. They emerge into daylight with another envelope and one more reason to believe the shoes will always save them.
beats.objective: Visit Second Spin Laundry and continue the New Turf route.

beats.title: New Turf · The Fence Lot
beats.summary: A fenced lot makes the route’s danger impossible to ignore.
paragraphs: Parked cars crowd the lanes inside the fence. The local crew refuses to pay. Then a dark car passes outside, shots interrupt the argument, and everyone scatters.
Malik brings Harold out of the confusion. For a moment, Harold sees the teenager who just saved him. Malik checks the envelope instead. Survival has started to feel routine to him.
beats.objective: Find the entrance to Railside Yard for the next New Turf scene.

beats.title: New Turf · The Hallway
beats.summary: Watching neighbors see how little space Malik leaves for anyone else.
paragraphs: The final stop runs along an apartment hallway. Neighbors watch from half-open doors while another local leader blocks the way. A struggle brings Malik dangerously close to the stairs.

He leaves with the envelope and an anger that survives the encounter. In the car, Harold thanks him for the earlier rescue. Malik tells the older man to fend for himself. The partnership has changed, and Harold hears it.
beats.objective: Return to the walkups’ hallway approach and finish the New Turf route.

beats.title: Positions
beats.summary: Malik brings back $25,000 and demands half. The organization answers with its hierarchy.
paragraphs: At the headquarters dice circle, Malik opens the bag in public: $25,000. He says he wants fifty percent. The yard goes quiet.
Mr. GREAT asks Harold to explain the operation. Harold names Low-Ski’s dice work, enforcement, logistics, and security. The speech is buying time while people at the crowd’s edges move into position.

Malik is killed. Harold removes the Robbery 1s from his feet. Mr. GREAT sends everyone back to their roles, and the dice begin moving again. The pair has a new keeper; the cost has fallen on Malik and the people who loved him.
beats.objective: Return to Night Shift Club and hear the organization’s answer.

beats.title: The Altar
beats.summary: Harold brings the original pair to Malik’s funeral. The pastor recognizes them.
paragraphs: At Malik’s funeral, Mama sits before a closed casket. Classmates, neighbors, Harold, and members of the organization occupy the same church. The pastor speaks about the kind of temptation that looks like help while it takes a life apart.
Harold walks forward and places the Robbery 1s at the altar. He confesses what he knows about the curse and what he watched it do to Malik. He is afraid of being the next person it takes.
The pastor kneels beside the shoes. Recognition changes his face. He says, “This was my first pair.” The story ends there, with the meaning of that recognition still unresolved.
beats.objective: Reach Second Light Chapel and hear the final scene.
